name: Small Property Manager Operations
audience: independent residential property managers and small property teams
topic: maintenance and turnover operations for small rental portfolios

products.name: Maintenance Triage Board
products.product: A lightweight intake and routing queue for maintenance requests across a small rental portfolio.
products.audience: independent residential property managers and small property teams
products.problem: Maintenance requests arrive through calls, texts, email, and tenant portals with inconsistent details, making urgency and ownership hard to assess.
products.valueProposition: Standardizes request evidence, urgency, access, vendor ownership, tenant updates, and completion confirmation.
products.monetization: $19-$79/month based on active records or team size
products.startupCost: Static product probe, managed database, email integration, and lightweight scheduled jobs.
products.seoAngle: Targets maintenance request triage template, landlord maintenance tracker, property manager work order spreadsheet, and tenant repair intake searches.

products.name: Unit Turnover Runbook
products.product: A dependency-aware checklist for coordinating inspections, repairs, cleaning, photos, and listing readiness between tenancies.
products.audience: independent residential property managers and small property teams
products.problem: Turnover tasks live in separate vendor texts and checklists, so one missed dependency can delay listing or move-in readiness.
products.valueProposition: Makes task dependencies, evidence, vendor dates, blockers, and final readiness visible for every vacant unit.
products.topic: rental unit turnover checklist and make-ready tracking
products.monetization: $19-$79/month based on active records or team size
products.startupCost: Static product probe, managed database, email integration, and lightweight scheduled jobs.
products.seoAngle: Targets apartment turnover checklist, rental make-ready template, property turnover tracker, and unit inspection workflow searches.
